data.name: Sudha
data.gender_notes: Sudha is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit sudhā, 'nectar, ambrosia'. Its root is Sanskrit sudhā (सुधा). A classical Sanskrit term for nectar. Sudha is a Sanskrit name meaning “Nectar; ambrosia; honey”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sudha expresses “Nectar; ambrosia; honey”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sudha total 17, reducing to 8. Number 8 is associated with ambition, authority and material mastery.

data.cultural_impact: Sudha is used in Sanskrit naming tradition with the meaning “Nectar; ambrosia; honey”.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning “Nectar; ambrosia; honey” is the basis of any symbolism attached to Sudha; such symbolism is interpretive.

vedic_reference.note: Refers to the purity, clarity, and brightness. In Hindu mythology, the goddess Saraswati is also referred to as Sudha.

historical_references.reference: A classical Sanskrit term for nectar.
